Cyclone Murasu tracker: Where is the storm?
articles.description: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu is approaching the south Andhra Pradesh coast, with landfall expected between Nellore and Narsapur around midnight on November 2 or during the early hours of November 3. As the state prepares for the storm, Tamil Nadu has sent 500 electricity department personnel to help restore power supply, while three National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams comprising 90 personnel have been deployed for rescue and relief operations.Tamil Nadu Electricity Minister R Nirmal Kumar said on Monday that the state had organised 25 teams of electricity department personnel to assist Andhra Pradesh following a request from Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu. The teams will help restore electricity supply disrupted by the cyclone.The India Meteorological Department (IMD), in its latest bulletin, said Murasu was moving west-northwestwards at 14 kmph over the west-central Bay of Bengal. The severe cyclonic storm is expected to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast with wind speeds of 100–110 kmph and gusts reaching 120 kmph.Also Read: Weather today, November 2: IMD warns of heavy rain in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu; Delhi-NCR's AQI becomes 'severe'; check latest IMD update and AQI levels— Indiametdept (@Indiametdept) Cyclone Murasu tracker: Latest storm position and movementThe IMD said the severe cyclonic storm was centred approximately 120 km east-southeast of Nellore, 140 km east-southeast of Kavali, 170 km northeast of Chennai, 180 km southeast of Ongole and 220 km south of Machilipatnam.The system had moved west-northwestwards at a speed of 14 kmph during the preceding six hours. The weather agency has forecast that it will continue moving northwestwards before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast.Cyclone Murasu landfall: Andhra Pradesh braces for winds up to 120 kmphAccording to the IMD forecast, Murasu is likely to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, around midnight on November 2 and during the early hours of November 3.The cyclone is expected to bring sustained wind speeds of 100–110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph during landfall. Its movement is being monitored by Doppler Weather Radars at Chennai, Machilipatnam and Visakhapatnam.Tamil Nadu sends 500 electricity personnel to restore power supplyTamil Nadu has deployed 500 electricity department personnel, divided into 25 teams, to help Andhra Pradesh restore electricity connections affected by Cyclone Murasu.Electricity Minister R Nirmal Kumar said the deployment followed a request from Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu. The teams will assist with power restoration as the neighbouring state prepares for the cyclone's impact.Three NDRF teams deployed from Arakkonam for rescue operationsThree NDRF teams comprising 90 personnel have been sent from the force's 4th Battalion near Arakkonam in Tamil Nadu to assist Andhra Pradesh with disaster management.Each team consists of 30 personnel. The teams are being deployed to areas including Nellore, Prakasam and Markapuram, where they will support emergency rescue and relief operations.According to officials, the teams, led by a senior commander, will undertake rescue work, clear debris and provide assistance to people affected by the cyclone.Cyclone Murasu: Heavy rainfall warning for OdishaThe southern districts of Odisha are likely to receive heavy rainfall ranging from 7 cm to 20 cm on November 2 and 3. Wind speeds of 50–60 kmph, with gusts reaching 70 kmph, are also forecast over parts of the state on November 3.The NDRF and Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) have been kept on standby in vulnerable areas. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea between November 2 and 4.In Ganjam district, officials were directed to stock essential supplies and move residents in high-risk locations to designated shelters by Sunday night, November 1, as part of preparations ahead of the cyclone.
